questions.q: The fractional change in the magnetic field intensity at a distance <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>r</mi></math> from centre on the axis of current carrying coil of radius <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>a</mi></math> to the magnetic field intensity at the centre of the same coil is: (Take <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">r</mi><mo><</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">a</mi></math>)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As we know,

Baxis=μ0iR22R2+x23/2  where, R=a  

Bcentre =μ0i2a

∴Baxis =μ0ia22a2+r23/2

∴ fractional change in magnetic field =μ0i2a-μ0ia22a2+r23/2μ0i2a=1-11+r2a23/2

≈1−1−32r2a2=32r2a2

questions.q: Two long straight wires <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>Q</mi></math> carrying equal current <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> each were kept parallel to each other at <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> distance. Magnitude of magnetic force experienced by <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> length of wire <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi></math> is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>F</mi><mn mathvariant="italic">1</mn></msub></math>. If distance between wires is halved and currents on them are doubled, force <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>F</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> on <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> length of wire <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>P</mi></math> will be:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As we know, force per unit length between two parallel straight wires is given by, F=μ0i1i22πd.

Therefore, required ratio

F1 F2=μ0(10)22π(5×10-2)μ0(20)22π52×10-2=18

⇒F2=8F1

questions.q: Two bar magnets oscillate in a horizontal plane in earth's magnetic field with time periods of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mo> </mo></math>respectively. If their moments of inertia are in the ratio of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mo>:</mo><mn>2</mn></math> then the ratio of their magnetic moments will be
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Torque on a bar magnet kept in a magnetic field is given by τ=MBsinθ.

Hence, for small oscillations the time period of bar magnets is given by,

T=2πIMB⇒M∝IT2

⇒M1M2=I1I2×T2T12

⇒M1M2=32×432=83

questions.q: A bar magnet having a magnetic moment of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>2</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>5</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">J</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>, is placed along the direction of uniform magnetic field of magnitude <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>14</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></math>. The work done in rotating the magnet slowly through <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>60</mn><mo>°</mo></math> from the direction of field is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Work done by the external force is equal to the change in the potential energy,

Wext=ΔU=Uf-Ui

⇒Wext=-MBcosθ2+MBcosθ1

⇒Wext=MBcosθ1-cosθ2

⇒Wext=14×10-5×2×105cos0°-cos60°

⇒Wext=14×2×12=14 J

questions.q:
A coil is placed in magnetic field such that plane of coil is perpendicular to the direction of magnetic field. The magnetic flux through a coil can be changed:

A. By changing the magnitude of the magnetic field within the coil.

B. By changing the area of coil within the magnetic field.

C. By changing the angle between the direction of magnetic field and the plane of the coil.

D. By reversing the magnetic field direction abruptly without changing its magnitude.

Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Magnetic flux through a coil is given by ϕ=B→.A→=BAcosθ, where,Bis magnetic field, A is area of coil and θ is the angle between B and A.

Thus, from above expression, we can say that magnetic flux can be changed by changing magnetic field, area of coil, change the angle between B and A.

Hence, correct options are A, B and C.

questions.q: An electron gun is placed inside a long solenoid of radius R on its axis. The solenoid has n turns/length and carries a current I. The electron gun shoots an electron along the radius of the solenoid with speed v. If the electron does not hit the surface of the solenoid, maximum possible value of v is (all symbols have their standard meaning):
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Magnetic Field Inside Solenoid is B=μ0nI

Velocity ν has given to the electron 

So, Magnetic Force

F=qνB

as ν and B are perpendicular.

In a magnetic field, charge will move on a circular path. Here, If radius is just less than or equal to radius of solenoid then the electron does not hit the surface.

F=qνB=mν2R⇒mν=qBRas  q=eν=eBRmSo,V=eμ0nIRm

The coil deflects by <math><msup><mrow><mn>1</mn></mrow><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">o</mi></mrow></msup></math> for a current of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mi> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi></math> The value of B (in tesla) is approximately:
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
$\mathrm{ppm}($ parts per million $)=\frac{\mathrm{mg} \text { of solute }}{\mathrm{L} \text { of solution }}$
Given,
$\mathrm{ppm}=1000\begin{aligned} & \text { volume }=1 \mathrm{~L} \\ & \mathrm{mg} \text { of solute }=\mathrm{ppm} \times \mathrm{L} \text { of solution } \\ & =10^3 \times 1 \\ & \text { weight of solute }=10^3 \mathrm{mg}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & \text { Concentration }=\frac{\text { no. of moles }}{\text { volume }} \\ & \text { no. of moles }=\frac{\text { weight of solute }}{\text { molecular weight of solute }}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} & =\frac{10^3 \times 10^{-3} \mathrm{~g}}{100 \mathrm{~g} \mathrm{~mol}^{-1}}\left[1 \mathrm{mg}=10^{-3} \mathrm{~g}\right] \\ & =10^{-2} \mathrm{~mol}\end{aligned}$
Concentration (c) $=\frac{10^{-2} \mathrm{~mol}}{1 \mathrm{~L}}=10^{-2} \mathrm{~mol} \mathrm{~L}^{-1}$

questions.q:
Uniform magnetic fields of different strengths $\left(B_1\right.$ and $B_2$), both normal to the plane of the paper exist as shown in the figure. A charged particle of mass m and charge q , at the interface at an instant, moves into the region 2 with velocity $v$ and returns to the interface. It continues to move into region 1 and finally reaches the interface. What is the displacement of the particle during this movement along the interface?

(Consider the velocity of the particle to be normal to the magnetic field and $B_2 \gt B_1$)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{v}}$ is $\perp$ to $\overrightarrow{\mathrm{B}}$, so charge particle will move in circular path, whose radius is given by
$\mathrm{R}=\frac{\mathrm{mv}}{\mathrm{qB}}$

Starting point $\rightarrow \mathrm{A}$
Ending point $\rightarrow \mathrm{C}$
$\therefore$ Net displacement $=\mathrm{AC}$
$\begin{aligned} & \mathrm{AC}=\mathrm{CD}-\mathrm{AD} \\ & \mathrm{AC}=\frac{2 \mathrm{mv}}{\mathrm{qB}_1}-\frac{2 \mathrm{mv}}{\mathrm{qB}_2} \\ & \mathrm{AC}=\frac{2 \mathrm{mv}}{\mathrm{qB}_1}\left[1-\frac{\mathrm{B}_1}{\mathrm{~B}_2}\right]\end{aligned}$

As magnetic moment of both the coil is the same,

μ1=μ2

⇒NAIAπrA2=NBIBπrB22⇒NAIA0.102=NBIB0.202⇒IANA=4IBNB

questions.q: A bar magnet with a magnetic moment <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>5</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math> is placed in parallel position relative to a magnetic field of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>4</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></math>. The amount of required work done in turning the magnet form parallel to antiparallel position relative to the field direction is ________.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For a bar magnet, the work done in turning from parallel to antiparallel position relative to the field direction is 

W=MBcosθ1-cosθ2, here, θ1=0° and θ1=180°.

W=-MBcos180°-mBcos0°

W=2 MB=2×5×0.4=4 J

questions.q: A charge of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo> </mo><mi>μ</mi><mi mathvariant="normal">C</mi></math> is moving with a velocity of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>4</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>0</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mn>6</mn></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math> along the positive <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>y</mi></math>-axis under a magnetic field <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>B</mi></math> of strength <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>(</mo><mn>2</mn><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">k</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo>)</mo><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi></math>. The force acting on the charge is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi><mover><mi mathvariant="normal">i</mi><mo>^</mo></mover><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">N</mi></math>. The value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> is ______.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Given:

q=4 μC,v→=4×106 j^ m s-1 and B→=2 k^ T

Force acting on charged particle, F→=q(v→×B→)

=4×10-64×106 j^×2 k^

=4×10-6×8×106i^

⇒F→=32 i^ N

⇒x=32

questions.q: Two long parallel wires $X$ and $Y$, separated by a distance of 6 cm , carry currents of 5A and 4A, respectively, in opposite directions as shown in the figure. Magnitude of the resultant magnetic field at point P at a distance of 4 cm from wire Y is $x \times 10^{-5} \mathrm{~T}$. The value of $x$ is__________ . Take permeability of free space as $\mu_0=4 \pi \times 10^{-7} \mathrm{SI}$ units.

questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} & B=\frac{\mu_0(5)}{2 \pi \times .01}-\frac{\mu_0 4}{2 \pi \times 0.04} \\ & =-\frac{100 \mu_0}{4 \pi} \\ & =-100 \times 10^{-7} \\ & =-1 \times 10^{-5} \mathrm{~T}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: The magnetic potential due to a magnetic dipole at a point on its axis situated at a distance of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>20</mn><mo> </mo><mi>cm</mi></math> from its center is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>1</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>×</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>5</mn></mrow></msup><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>. The magnetic moment of the dipole is _______ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mn>2</mn></msup></math>. (Given : <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfrac><msub><mi>μ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mrow><mn>4</mn><mi>π</mi></mrow></mfrac><mo>=</mo><msup><mn>10</mn><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>7</mn><mo> </mo></mrow></msup><mi mathvariant="normal">T</mi><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">A</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>)
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The formula to calculate the magnetic potential due to a magnetic dipole can be written as

V=μ04πMr2   ...1

Substitute the values of the known parameters into equation (1) and solve to calculate the required magnetic moment of the dipole.

1.5×10-5=10-7×M20×10-22⇒M=1.5×10-5×20×20×10-410-7⇒M=1.5×4=6 A m2
